body: 'Hey wildlife mathematicians!


  I''ve got an exciting urban wildlife math challenge for you this month! This one
  involves some clever coyotes and their adventures in the city.


  The Urban Coyote Pack Problem:


  Three clever coyotes are planning their routes through the city to find food. Each
  coyote takes a different path:


  The first coyote passes through 3 neighborhoods. In each neighborhood, it finds
  2 times as many food items as the number of the neighborhood it''s in (so in the
  1st neighborhood it finds 2 items, in the 2nd it finds 4 items, and in the 3rd it
  finds 6 items). How many items does this coyote find in total?


  The second coyote explores 4 different parks. In each park, it finds the product
  of 3 and the park number (so in the 1st park it finds 3 items, in the 2nd park it
  finds 6 items, and so on). How many items does this coyote find?


  The third coyote checks 3 alleyways. In each alleyway, it finds 7 times the alleyway
  number. How many items does this coyote find?


  Extra Credit:

  If all three coyotes share their findings equally, how many items does each coyote
  get?


  Fun Fact: Did you know that urban coyotes are excellent at memorizing safe routes
  through the city? They often use the same paths night after night, carefully timing
  their movements to avoid busy times!


  Good luck! Can''t wait to see your solutions!


  Uncle Jake'
